title: Remote Visual Tracking Using Semantic Scene Understanding and GenAI-based Predictive Rendering Under Disaster Situation
summary: TCS proposes semantic scene understanding and generative rendering to help disaster responders share visual information under bandwidth constraints.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The concept seeks to reconstruct useful visual scenes from compact transmitted information. TCS states that it is not fully deployed and that more suitable datasets are needed. Faster disaster response and reduced consequences are intended benefits, without an observed response or rescue outcome.
purpose: Share actionable visual information during constrained disaster communications.
system: Remote Visual Tracking Using Semantic Scene Understanding and GenAI-based Predictive Rendering Under Disaster Situation

ratings.reason: The disaster-tracking concept is not fully deployed and still requires a suitable dataset; no response improvement is documented.
No rescue or avoided injury is attributed to the system.
Reduced disaster impact is a potential effect.

ai_role.statement: The contributor describes the system and its proposed or reported contribution. This collection entry does not independently isolate the effect of AI from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 14: Remote Visual Tracking Using Semantic Scene Understanding and GenAI-based Predictive Rendering Under Disaster Situation

produced_by: The contributor describes the application and its setting in the cited entry. Conditions sufficient to reproduce the reported benefit have not been established.
must_hold: Requirements for reproducing the benefit need to be evaluated in the new setting. The collection entry does not establish that its reported results will recur.
